selected_hotel.name: Djemaa el-Fna, Medina, Marrakech Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Djemaa el-Fna Square & Medina Exploration
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in the beating heart of Marrakech by exploring the UNESCO-listed Djemaa el-Fna square. Watch snake charmers, storytellers, and musicians by day, then witness the square transform into a massive open-air food market at dusk. Wander through the labyrinthine souks of the old medina, haggling for spices, leather goods, and handwoven textiles.

experiences.name: Sahara Desert Camel Trek & Overnight Camp
experiences.description: Ride a camel into the golden dunes of Erg Chebbi near Merzouga for a truly unforgettable adventure. Watch the sunset paint the dunes in shades of amber and red, then spend the night in a traditional Berber desert camp under a breathtaking canopy of stars. Wake before dawn to catch the sunrise over the Sahara — one of the most magical experiences on earth.

experiences.name: Bahia Palace & Saadian Tombs Historical Tour
experiences.description: Step back in time with a self-guided or local-guided tour of two of Marrakech's most stunning historical sites. The 19th-century Bahia Palace dazzles with its intricate zellige tilework, carved cedarwood ceilings, and lush gardens. A short walk away, the Saadian Tombs — sealed for centuries and rediscovered in 1917 — house the ornately decorated mausoleums of the Saadian dynasty.

experiences.name: Traditional Moroccan Cooking Class
experiences.description: Join a hands-on cooking class in a riad kitchen and learn to prepare iconic Moroccan dishes such as lamb tagine, chicken bastilla, and fresh harira soup. Begin with a guided tour of the spice souks to select fresh ingredients like ras el hanout, preserved lemons, and saffron. End the session by sitting down together to enjoy the feast you've created — a deeply cultural and delicious experience.

experiences.name: Todra Gorge Hike & Berber Village Visit
experiences.description: En route to or from the Sahara, stop at the dramatic Todra Gorge — towering 300-meter canyon walls carved by the Todra River. Hike through the narrow gorge passages and explore the lush palm oasis at its base. Visit a nearby Berber village to experience traditional mud-brick architecture, share mint tea with locals, and gain insight into the ancient semi-nomadic culture of the Atlas region.
experiences.location: Todra Gorge, Tinghir Province, High Atlas

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Djemaa el-Fna, Medina, Marrakech Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Marrakech Menara Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Take a petit taxi (negotiate to ~50-70 MAD) or shared bus (Bus 19, ~4 MAD) to your riad in the Medina near Djemaa el-Fna. Check in, freshen up, and orient yourself with a short walk around the immediate neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: First immersion into Djemaa el-Fna Square — explore the iconic open-air square at its afternoon peak. Watch snake charmers, henna artists, and street performers. Stroll into the adjacent Souk Semmarine for a gentle introduction to the labyrinthine souks. Browse spices, leather goods, and lanterns without pressure to buy on day one.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Djemaa el-Fna as the square transforms into a massive open-air food market. Dozens of stalls fire up grills — this is the most atmospheric (and cheapest) dinner in Marrakech. Watch the storytellers and Gnawa musicians perform under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a coffee and msemen (Moroccan flatbread) from a street cart near the airport for ~10 MAD
meals.lunch: Grab a sandwich or harira soup from a hole-in-the-wall café near Djemaa el-Fna after check-in (~20-30 MAD)
meals.dinner: Djemaa el-Fna night market food stalls — try brochettes, merguez sausage, snail soup (babouche), and fresh orange juice. Full meal for ~50-70 MAD

day_by_day.notes: Arrival day — keep it light. Exchange some cash at the airport or a bureau de change in the Medina (avoid hotel exchange rates). Carry small bills for tipping and street food. The Medina is best explored on foot — wear comfortable shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Early visit to the Koutoubia Mosque gardens (exterior only for non-Muslims, free) at sunrise for stunning light and fewer crowds. Then head to the Bahia Palace (~70 MAD entry) — one of Marrakech's most ornate 19th-century palaces with stunning Andalusian-Moorish architecture, zellige tilework, and carved cedar ceilings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the El Badi Palace ruins (~70 MAD entry) — a hauntingly beautiful 16th-century ruined palace with resident storks nesting on the battlements. Afterward, explore the Mellah (Jewish Quarter) with its distinctive yellow-painted buildings and the Lazama Synagogue (small donation appreciated). Browse the spice souk and Rahba Kedima (Place des Épices).
day_by_day.evening: Take a rooftop café sunset view over the Medina — Café Arabe or Nomad offer stunning panoramas. Then wander back to Djemaa el-Fna for evening entertainment and street food.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Moroccan breakfast at your riad or a nearby café — mint tea, msemen, amlou (argan oil dip), honey (~30-40 MAD)
meals.lunch: Cheap local lunch at a Mellah neighborhood restaurant — tagine or couscous with bread (~40-60 MAD)
meals.dinner: Street food at Djemaa el-Fna or a budget medina restaurant — try pastilla (pigeon pie) or kefta tagine (~50-80 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Start early to beat the heat and tourist crowds at the palaces. The Bahia and El Badi palaces are a 10-minute walk from each other. Bargaining is expected in the souks — start at 30-40% of the asking price. Keep your bag zipped in crowded areas.

day_by_day.morning: Deep dive into the historic souks — hire a local guide for a 2-hour souk tour (~150-200 MAD, negotiate) or explore independently. Visit the Souk des Teinturiers (Dyers' Quarter) to see vibrant wool being dyed in open vats — a photographer's dream. Also explore Souk Cherratine (leather workers) and Souk Haddadine (blacksmiths).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Ben Youssef Madrasa (~70 MAD) — a 14th-century Quranic school considered one of the most beautiful buildings in Morocco, with intricate stucco, zellige, and carved cedar. Then head to the Marrakech Museum in the nearby Mnebhi Palace (~50 MAD) for Moroccan art and artifacts.
day_by_day.evening: Hammam experience at a traditional local hammam (not a tourist spa) — Hammam Dar el-Bacha or a neighborhood hammam (~50-80 MAD for basic scrub and steam). Finish with dinner at a local restaurant away from the main square for better prices.

meals.breakfast: Café des Épices near Rahba Kedima — coffee, juice, and Moroccan pancakes with a rooftop view (~35 MAD)
meals.lunch: Snack from souk vendors — fresh-squeezed orange juice (4 MAD!), roasted almonds, and a khobz sandwich (~25-30 MAD)
meals.dinner: Restaurant Haj Brik near Djemaa el-Fna — beloved by locals for cheap, authentic Moroccan food. Harira, tagine, and bread for ~60 MAD

day_by_day.notes: The Ben Youssef Madrasa is the cultural highlight of Marrakech — arrive before 10am for the best light through the central courtyard. Wear modest clothing (shoulders and knees covered) for religious and cultural sites. The hammam is a quintessential Moroccan experience — bring flip-flops and a change of clothes.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Atlas Mountains and Berber villages — join a budget shared group tour (~200-300 MAD) departing from Djemaa el-Fna. Visit the Ourika Valley or the Imlil trailhead village. Enjoy dramatic mountain scenery, terraced fields, and authentic Berber hospitality. Short hike to a waterfall in the Ourika Valley if conditions allow.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Atlas foothills — visit a Berber family home for mint tea (often included in tours or ~20-30 MAD tip). Browse a cooperative selling Berber carpets and argan oil products. Return to Marrakech by late afternoon (tours typically return 17:00-18:00).
day_by_day.evening: Relax after the day trip. Explore the quieter northern Medina neighborhoods around Bab Doukkala gate. Visit a local pharmacy-herbalist in the souks for Moroccan beauty products and spices to take home.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at your riad before the early departure (~30 MAD or included)
meals.lunch: Tagine lunch at a Berber restaurant in the Atlas Mountains — often included in tours or ~60-80 MAD separately. Stunning mountain backdrop.
meals.dinner: Budget restaurant near Djemaa el-Fna — try tanjia (Marrakchi slow-cooked lamb) — a dish unique to this city (~70-90 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Atlas Mountains group tour the evening before from agencies around Djemaa el-Fna — shop around for the best price. Bring a light jacket as mountain temperatures are cooler than the city, especially in March. This is a great cultural contrast to the urban Medina experience.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure for the Sahara Desert — take a budget shared CTM or Supratours bus from Marrakech to Ouarzazate (~80-100 MAD, ~3.5 hours) via the dramatic Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass (2260m). The drive through the High Atlas is spectacular. Arrive in Ouarzazate mid-morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Ouarzazate — the 'Hollywood of Africa.' Visit Aït Benhaddou (~10 MAD entry), a UNESCO World Heritage ksar (fortified village) used in Game of Thrones, Gladiator, and Lawrence of Arabia. Climb to the top for panoramic views of the kasbah and surrounding desert landscape. Wander through the lower village and cross the river on foot.
day_by_day.evening: Check into a budget guesthouse in Ouarzazate (~150-200 MAD for a dorm or basic room). Stroll through the town center, visit the local market, and enjoy a quiet desert-town evening. Prepare for tomorrow's Sahara adventure.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your riad before the bus departure (~30 MAD)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from a Ouarzazate market or a café near Aït Benhaddou — sandwiches and fruit (~30-40 MAD)
meals.dinner: Local restaurant in Ouarzazate — try mechoui (slow-roasted lamb) or a simple tagine (~50-70 MAD). The town has excellent budget eateries.

day_by_day.notes: Book the bus ticket at least a day in advance from the CTM or Supratours office near Djemaa el-Fna. The Tizi n'Tichka pass can be cold and occasionally snowy in March — bring a jacket. Aït Benhaddou is best visited in the afternoon light. Alternatively, book a shared desert tour from Marrakech that includes transport and overnight camping (~500-700 MAD total).

day_by_day.morning: Travel deeper into the Sahara — take a shared taxi or join a budget group tour from Ouarzazate toward Merzouga and the Erg Chebbi dunes (~150-200 MAD shared taxi, ~4-5 hours). Pass through the stunning Draa Valley, Agdz, Zagora, and the pre-Saharan landscape of palmeries and ancient kasbahs. Stop at Tamnougalt Kasbah if passing through.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Merzouga and the Erg Chebbi — the iconic orange sand dunes rising up to 150 meters. Check into a budget desert camp or guesthouse (~150-250 MAD). Rent a camel or walk to the base of the dunes. Explore the dune edges and nearby nomad settlements. Visit a Gnawa music community near Merzouga village.
day_by_day.evening: Camel trek into the Sahara at sunset (~100-150 MAD for 1-hour trek) — ride to a traditional Berber desert camp for an unforgettable night under the stars. Enjoy a campfire dinner with Berber music, drumming, and stargazing in one of the world's darkest skies. Sleep in a traditional nomad tent.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at guesthouse in Ouarzazate before departure (~25-35 MAD)
meals.lunch: Roadside café stop en route — harira soup and bread (~25-30 MAD)
meals.dinner: Traditional Berber camp dinner — tagine, bread, mint tea, and fresh fruit around the campfire (usually included in camp fee or ~80-100 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: March is ideal Sahara weather — warm days (25-28°C) and cool nights (8-12°C). Bring a warm layer for the overnight camp. Negotiate camel trek and camp prices before agreeing — budget camps offer excellent value. The Milky Way is extraordinarily visible from the Sahara in March. Bring a headlamp, sunscreen, and a scarf to protect from sand.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before dawn for a magical Sahara sunrise from the top of the dunes — the light turns the sand from deep purple to burning orange. Take a final walk or camel ride back to the guesthouse. Freshen up, pack, and begin the long journey back to Marrakech via shared taxi or a pre-arranged group return transfer (~200-250 MAD). The return journey offers different scenery via the Ziz Valley and Todra Gorge if time allows.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive back in Marrakech by late afternoon (plan for a 6-7 hour return journey). Drop bags at the riad and do any last-minute souvenir shopping in the souks — leather slippers (babouches), argan oil, spices, and Berber rugs are the best buys. Visit the Mellah spice market for the best prices on cumin, ras el hanout, and saffron.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Marrakech — return to Djemaa el-Fna one last time for the full sensory experience. Enjoy a final Moroccan dinner, watch the entertainers, and sip fresh orange juice as the call to prayer echoes across the square. A perfect farewell to Morocco.

meals.breakfast: Sunrise breakfast at the desert camp — Moroccan flatbread, olive oil, honey, and mint tea (included or ~20 MAD)
meals.lunch: Roadside stop en route back — tagine or sandwich at a local café (~35-50 MAD)
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly on your last night — try Restaurant Earth Café (vegetarian-friendly) or Café Clock near Djemaa el-Fna for a memorable farewell meal (~80-120 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Allow plenty of time for the return journey — Moroccan shared taxis wait until full before departing. If you have an early flight the next day, consider booking a private transfer back (~300-400 MAD split between travelers). Exchange remaining dirhams before leaving Morocco as MAD is not easily convertible abroad. Keep some cash for tips — guides, drivers, and camp staff appreciate 20-50 MAD.

trip_options.title: Classic Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Djemaa el-Fna, Medina, Marrakech Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Marrakech Menara Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer to your boutique riad in the Medina near Djemaa el-Fna (approx. 20–30 min by taxi, ~80–100 MAD). Check in, freshen up, and settle into your accommodation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle orientation walk around Djemaa el-Fna square and its immediate surroundings. Explore the edges of the souks near Rue des Épices, visit the nearby Koutoubia Mosque gardens (exterior), and get your bearings in the Medina. Pick up a local SIM card from a nearby phone shop if needed.
day_by_day.evening: Experience the magic of Djemaa el-Fna at dusk — watch the square transform with snake charmers, storytellers, musicians, and food stalls. Head to a rooftop café overlooking the square (Café de France or Café Argana) for mint tea and the panoramic view. Stroll back for an early dinner and rest after travel.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or grab a light snack at the airport upon arrival
meals.lunch: Light meal at a café near the riad after check-in — try a harira soup and msemen (Moroccan flatbread) at a local café for ~30–50 MAD
meals.dinner: Dinner at a mid-range restaurant on or near Djemaa el-Fna — try Earth Café or Le Marrakchi for tagine or couscous (150–220 MAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light given the afternoon arrival. Prioritize rest to recover from travel. Keep your valuables secure in the busy square. Bargain politely if approached by vendors.

day_by_day.morning: Full morning exploring the historic Medina. Visit the stunning Bahia Palace (entry ~70 MAD) — a 19th-century grand vizier's palace with intricate Moroccan craftsmanship. Then walk to the nearby Mellah (Jewish Quarter) and the old Bab Mellah gate to soak in layers of history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the famous souks of Marrakech — navigate through the dyers' souk (Souk Sabbaghin), spice souk, leather souk, and the lamp souk. Visit the Ben Youssef Madrasa (entry ~70 MAD), a breathtaking 14th-century Islamic college with stunning zellige tilework and carved stucco. End at the nearby Marrakech Museum housed in the Dar Menebhi Palace.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Djemaa el-Fna for the full evening spectacle. Dine at the open-air food stalls in the center of the square (stalls numbered 1–100) — a quintessential Marrakech experience. Try grilled merguez, brochettes, snail soup, and fresh-squeezed orange juice (budget-friendly: 80–150 MAD for a full meal).

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your riad (typically included) or a local café — café au lait, msemen with honey and argan oil, and fresh orange juice (~40 MAD if not included)
meals.lunch: Snack lunch in the souks — fresh-squeezed juice (10 MAD), a sandwich or fried fish near Souk Kchacha (~40–60 MAD)
meals.dinner: Djemaa el-Fna food stalls — full grilled meal with sides and fresh juice (~80–150 MAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — you'll cover 5–8 km today. The Medina can be disorienting; use Google Maps offline or a local guide app. Bargaining in the souks is expected — start at 40–50% of the asking price.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Saadian Tombs (entry ~70 MAD) — a royal necropolis dating to the 16th century rediscovered in 1917, featuring ornate marble and cedarwood details. Afterward, explore the atmospheric El Badi Palace ruins (entry ~70 MAD), a once-magnificent 16th-century palace now hauntingly beautiful in its decay, with resident storks nesting on the battlements.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a short taxi ride (~20 min) to the Majorelle Garden and YSL Museum complex. Stroll through the iconic cobalt-blue Majorelle Garden designed by French painter Jacques Majorelle and later restored by Yves Saint Laurent (entry ~150 MAD). Visit the Berber Museum within the garden. The adjacent YSL Museum (entry ~100 MAD) is optional for fashion and design enthusiasts.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Gueliz neighborhood (New Town) for a different atmosphere — browse the art galleries and boutiques along Avenue Mohammed V. Enjoy dinner at a modern Moroccan restaurant in Gueliz for a refined experience.

meals.breakfast: Riad breakfast or local café near Djemaa el-Fna
meals.lunch: Café Bousafsaf or a café near Majorelle Garden — salads, sandwiches, and fresh juices (~80–120 MAD)
meals.dinner: Comptoir Darna or Kechmara in Gueliz — contemporary Moroccan cuisine with a relaxed atmosphere (~200–300 MAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book Majorelle Garden tickets online in advance — it sells out frequently, especially in spring. March is a beautiful time to visit as the garden is lush. Taxi from Medina to Majorelle is ~30–40 MAD (negotiate before getting in).

day_by_day.morning: Early departure (6:00–7:00 AM) for the Sahara Desert — begin the scenic drive over the High Atlas Mountains via the Tizi n'Tichka pass (2,260m elevation). Stop at the dramatic mountain scenery viewpoints along the way. Arrive in the UNESCO-listed Aït Benhaddou ksar (fortified village) — a stunning earthen citadel used in Game of Thrones, Gladiator, and Lawrence of Arabia. Explore the ksar on foot (entry ~20 MAD).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue driving through the Draa Valley and Dadès Gorge region toward Merzouga and the Erg Chebbi dunes. The landscape shifts dramatically from mountains to desert — red ochre kasbahs, date palm oases, and vast rocky hammada. Arrive in Merzouga village by late afternoon. Check into a mid-range desert camp or guesthouse.
day_by_day.evening: Mount a camel at sunset for a 45–60 minute ride into the Erg Chebbi dunes (included in most desert camp packages or ~200–300 MAD separately). Arrive at your Berber desert camp in time for sunset over the dunes — one of Morocco's most iconic experiences. Enjoy a traditional dinner around a campfire with Gnawa music.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the riad before departure
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or stop at a roadside restaurant in Ouarzazate — tagine or sandwich (~60–100 MAD)
meals.dinner: Traditional Berber dinner at the desert camp — included in most camp packages (harira, tagine, fresh bread, mint tea, and seasonal fruits)

day_by_day.notes: This is a long driving day (~8–10 hours total including stops). Book a private driver or organized day tour from Marrakech (mid-range: 600–900 MAD per person for a shared tour, or 1,500–2,000 MAD for a private car). Alternatively, join a 3-day organized Marrakech–Sahara tour. Bring layers — the desert is cold at night in March (can drop to 5–10°C).

day_by_day.morning: Wake before sunrise (around 6:30 AM) to climb the dunes for a spectacular Sahara sunrise — one of the most memorable moments of any Morocco trip. Watch the shifting colors of the dunes from gold to amber to pink. Return to camp for a traditional Berber breakfast. Optional: sandboarding on the dunes (boards available at camp or nearby rental shops, ~50–80 MAD).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Merzouga village and the surrounding area. Visit a local Gnawa musician's home for a cultural music session (often arranged by camps, ~50–100 MAD donation). Explore the fossil and mineral shops of Erfoud on the way back. Optional adventure: quad biking across the dunes (1 hour ~250–350 MAD) for adrenaline seekers.
day_by_day.evening: Begin the return journey toward Marrakech, stopping overnight in the Dadès Valley or Ouarzazate to break up the drive. Check into a mid-range guesthouse or kasbah hotel in the valley. Enjoy a quiet dinner and stargazing in the clear desert sky.

meals.breakfast: Berber breakfast at the desert camp — mint tea, msemen, honey, argan oil, and hard-boiled eggs
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local restaurant in Merzouga or Erfoud — tagine or grilled meat (~80–120 MAD)
meals.dinner: Dinner at your overnight guesthouse in the Dadès Valley — home-cooked Moroccan meal (~120–180 MAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: The sunrise experience is the highlight of the Sahara visit — set an alarm and don't miss it. Bring a headlamp for navigating the dunes in the dark. Apply sunscreen generously during the day as the desert sun is intense even in March.

day_by_day.morning: Morning exploration of the Dadès Gorge or Todra Gorge (depending on overnight location) — dramatic limestone canyon walls rising up to 300m. Take a short hike along the gorge floor (easy, 1–2 hours). The Todra Gorge is a popular rock-climbing destination and offers stunning photography opportunities in the morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive back over the Atlas Mountains toward Marrakech. Stop at a traditional Berber argan oil cooperative along the route — learn about the argan oil production process and support local Berber women's cooperatives (free to visit, purchase optional). Arrive back in Marrakech by late afternoon. Return to your riad, shower, and decompress.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed final evening in Marrakech — visit a traditional hammam for a cleansing steam bath and scrub (mid-range hammam: Hammam de la Rose or Les Bains de Marrakech, ~250–400 MAD for a full treatment). Follow with a leisurely dinner at one of Marrakech's finest riads or rooftop restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your overnight guesthouse in the Dadès Valley
meals.lunch: Roadside lunch on the return journey — stop at a local restaurant in Kalaat M'Gouna (Rose Valley) for tagine (~70–100 MAD)
meals.dinner: Splurge dinner at Dar Yacout or Nomad Restaurant in the Medina — a refined Moroccan dining experience (~250–400 MAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the hammam in advance, especially for Saturday evening as it can be busy. The Rose Valley (Kalaat M'Gouna) is famous for its rose festival in May — in March you'll see the roses beginning to bloom. A mid-range private driver for the full Sahara round trip (Days 4–6) typically costs 2,500–3,500 MAD total.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech — revisit your favorite spot in the Medina or explore anything you missed earlier in the week. Visit the Mellah spice market for last-minute souvenir shopping — saffron, ras el hanout spice blend, argan oil, and rose water make excellent gifts. Wander through the Souk Cherratine (leather souk) for leather goods at better prices than tourist shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Enjoy a leisurely lunch at a rooftop restaurant with views over the Medina. Pack your bags and prepare for departure. Depending on your flight time, arrange a taxi to Marrakech Menara Airport (allow 45–60 minutes for airport procedures). The airport is about 20–30 minutes from the Medina by taxi (~80–100 MAD).
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Marrakech — carry the memories of the Sahara dunes, Atlas Mountains, ancient kasbahs, and the vibrant chaos of Djemaa el-Fna with you.

meals.breakfast: Final riad breakfast — savor the mint tea, fresh pastries, and fruit one last time
meals.lunch: Rooftop lunch at Café des Épices or Nomad in the Medina — salads, sandwiches, and tagine with panoramic Medina views (~120–180 MAD)
meals.dinner: Airport meal or in-flight depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Allow extra time at Marrakech Menara Airport — security lines can be slow on Sundays. Keep some MAD for the taxi and any last-minute purchases. Duty-free at the airport offers argan products and Moroccan sweets at fair prices. Tipping culture: 10–15% at restaurants, 10–20 MAD for porters, 20–50 MAD for guides.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Djemaa el-Fna, Medina, Marrakech Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Marrakech Menara Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private transfer arranged from airport to your boutique riad in the Medina near Djemaa el-Fna. Check-in, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome mint tea ceremony at the riad.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle introduction to the Medina: a leisurely guided walk through the iconic Djemaa el-Fna square, taking in the atmosphere of snake charmers, storytellers, and street performers. Visit the nearby Koutoubia Mosque gardens for a peaceful stroll and orientation to the city. Browse the edge of the souks for a first sensory taste without the pressure of deep exploration.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset rooftop aperitif at your riad or a nearby rooftop terrace overlooking Djemaa el-Fna. Watch the square transform into its legendary night market as hundreds of food stalls light up. Dinner at a premium restaurant in the Medina.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — afternoon arrival
meals.lunch: Light welcome mezze and Moroccan pastries served at the riad upon check-in
meals.dinner: Dinner at Le Foundouk (Rue du Souk des Fassis) — a beautifully restored 18th-century caravanserai serving refined Moroccan cuisine; try the lamb pastilla and preserved lemon chicken tagine. Reserve in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 relaxed to recover from travel. Confirm your private driver and guide bookings for the coming days. Ask the riad concierge to arrange a hammam appointment for Day 2 morning. Dress modestly when walking in the Medina.

day_by_day.morning: Private traditional hammam and spa experience at a premium hammam such as Hammam de la Rose or Royal Mansour Spa (if accessible as a day guest). Full black soap scrub, ghassoul clay mask, and relaxation ritual — a quintessential Moroccan luxury experience lasting 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided tour of Marrakech's historic and cultural highlights: the ornate Bahia Palace (19th-century vizier's palace with stunning Andalusian courtyards), the hauntingly beautiful ruins of El Badi Palace (16th century), and the Saadian Tombs — royal mausoleums of extraordinary craftsmanship discovered in 1917. Your guide will provide rich historical context throughout.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Mellah (historic Jewish quarter) at dusk, then enjoy a premium dinner in a palatial riad setting with live Gnawa or Andalusian music.

meals.breakfast: Full Moroccan breakfast at your riad — msemen flatbreads, amlou (almond-argan dip), fresh-squeezed orange juice, honey, and Moroccan mint tea
meals.lunch: Lunch at Nomad Restaurant (Derb Aarjane, near the spice souks) — contemporary Moroccan cuisine with a stunning rooftop terrace; try the spiced lamb burger or roasted vegetable couscous
meals.dinner: Dinner at Dar Yacout (23 Sidi Ahmed Soussi) — one of Marrakech's most celebrated palatial dining experiences; multiple Moroccan courses in a 1001-nights setting with musicians; book well in advance

day_by_day.notes: Book the hammam and Dar Yacout well ahead of arrival. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the palace visits — cobblestone streets are uneven. The Saadian Tombs can be busy mid-morning; your private guide can time the visit to avoid peak crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided deep-dive into the historic souks of Marrakech: navigate the labyrinthine lanes of the dyers' souk (Souk Sabbaghin), the leather souk, the spice market (Rahba Kedima), and the woodworkers' quarter. Your guide will introduce you to master craftsmen and explain centuries-old techniques. Visit the Ben Youssef Madrasa — a stunning 16th-century Islamic school with intricate zellij tilework, carved stucco, and cedar wood ceilings (one of the finest in North Africa).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Musée de Marrakech housed in the 19th-century Mnebhi Palace, followed by a private visit to the Maison de la Photographie (House of Photography) for a curated collection of historical images of Morocco from 1870–1950. Afterward, a private cooking class at a premium riad kitchen — learn to make harira soup, tagine, and bastilla under the guidance of a Moroccan chef.
day_by_day.evening: Free evening to wander Djemaa el-Fna at your own pace and soak in the night market energy. Alternatively, the riad concierge can arrange a private rooftop dining experience.

meals.breakfast: Full Moroccan breakfast at the riad
meals.lunch: Lunch at Café des Épices (Rahba Kedima) — charming terrace overlooking the spice square; fresh salads, briouats, and Moroccan sandwiches
meals.dinner: Dinner at Dar Moha (81 Rue Dar el Bacha) — set in a stunning riad with a pool; Chef Mohammed Fedal's creative modern Moroccan cuisine is legendary; try the pigeon pastilla and lamb mechoui

day_by_day.notes: The cooking class typically runs 3–4 hours including the meal. Arrange this through your riad concierge for a premium private experience. In the souks, your guide will help with fair pricing if you wish to purchase crafts, textiles, or spices.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Marrakech early (around 07:00) by private luxury 4x4 vehicle for the journey to the Sahara Desert (Merzouga/Erg Chebbi). The drive takes approximately 8–9 hours with scenic stops. First stop: the dramatic Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass through the High Atlas Mountains (2,260m elevation) — breathtaking panoramic views and Berber villages clinging to cliffsides.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through the Anti-Atlas foothills, stopping at the UNESCO-listed fortified city of Aït Benhaddou — one of the world's most spectacular kasbahs, used as a filming location for Gladiator, Game of Thrones, and Lawrence of Arabia. Private guided tour of the ksar with a local Berber guide. Continue driving through the Valley of the Roses (Dadès Valley) and the dramatic Draa Valley with its ancient palm groves.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at the edge of Erg Chebbi dunes near Merzouga as the sun sets. Mount private camels for a guided sunset trek into the dunes, arriving at your exclusive luxury desert camp for the night.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast packed by the riad before departure — Moroccan pastries, fruit, and thermos of mint tea for the road
meals.lunch: Lunch stop at a quality restaurant in Ouarzazate — try the Kasbah Café or a restaurant near Aït Benhaddou for a tagine and fresh salad
meals.dinner: Traditional Berber dinner under the stars at your private luxury desert camp — slow-cooked lamb tagine, couscous, fresh salads, and Moroccan pastries; followed by a private Gnawa musician performance around the campfire

day_by_day.notes: This is a long driving day (8–9 hours total with stops) — start early to maximize daylight. Dress in layers; the High Atlas pass can be cold in March. Bring sunscreen and a scarf for the camel ride and dunes. Confirm the luxury camp booking (options: Scarabeo Camp or Erg Chebbi Luxury Camp) well in advance — these book out fast.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before dawn for a private sunrise camel trek or guided walk to the top of the highest dune at Erg Chebbi — watching the Sahara light up in gold, orange, and crimson is a once-in-a-lifetime experience. Return to camp for a full breakfast. Optional morning activity: private sandboarding on the dunes or a 4x4 dune-bashing excursion with an expert local driver.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a Berber nomad family encampment near the dunes for an authentic cultural exchange — share tea and learn about traditional desert life. Explore the small town of Merzouga and visit a fossil and mineral market unique to this region (the area is rich in Devonian-era marine fossils). Optional: visit the Dayet Srij salt lake nearby, which attracts flamingos in spring (March is a good season).
day_by_day.evening: Second night at the luxury desert camp or transfer to a premium kasbah hotel in Merzouga (such as Kasbah Mohayut or Riad Madu) for added comfort. Stargazing session with a private guide using a telescope — the Sahara offers some of the darkest skies in the world.

meals.breakfast: Full camp breakfast — eggs, msemen, fresh fruit, honey, argan oil, and mint tea served in the camp dining tent
meals.lunch: Light Berber lunch at camp or at a local café in Merzouga — harira soup, kefta brochettes, and fresh-baked bread
meals.dinner: Gourmet dinner at your kasbah or camp — mechoui (slow-roasted whole lamb), seven-vegetable couscous, and Moroccan sweets; paired with fresh-pressed juices

day_by_day.notes: March nights in the Sahara can drop to 5–10°C — pack a warm layer for the sunrise excursion and evening stargazing. The camel trek is approximately 45 minutes each way. Sandboarding boards are typically provided by the camp. Tip your Berber guides generously — this is their primary livelihood.

day_by_day.morning: Depart the desert after breakfast and begin the return journey to Marrakech via a different scenic route through the Draa Valley and the Skoura Oasis. Stop at Skoura to visit the famous Kasbah Amerhidil — one of the best-preserved kasbahs in Morocco — and walk through the ancient palm grove (palmeraie) with a local guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through Ouarzazate — the 'Hollywood of Africa' — and visit the Atlas Film Studios, the largest film studios in the world, where sets from major productions are preserved. Visit the Taourirt Kasbah in Ouarzazate, a UNESCO-listed fortress of the Glaoui clan. Depart Ouarzazate and drive over the Tizi n'Tichka pass back toward Marrakech, arriving by early evening.
day_by_day.evening: Return to your riad in Marrakech. Freshen up and enjoy a final premium evening in the city — a cocktail on a rooftop terrace followed by a celebratory dinner.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the desert camp or kasbah before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch in Ouarzazate at La Kasbah des Sables or a restaurant near the film studios — grilled meats, Moroccan salads, and fresh bread
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner at La Maison Arabe (1 Derb Assehbe, Bab Doukkala, Marrakech) — one of the city's most prestigious dining addresses; classic Moroccan haute cuisine in an exquisite riad setting with live traditional music

day_by_day.notes: The return drive is approximately 7–8 hours with stops — depart by 08:00 to arrive comfortably before dinner. The Atlas Film Studios tour takes about 1.5 hours. Confirm your riad reservation for the final night and request a late checkout for Day 7 if your flight allows.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech — a leisurely breakfast at the riad. Last-minute souvenir shopping in the souks: pick up premium argan oil products, hand-woven Berber carpets, Moroccan leather goods, or artisan ceramics. Visit the Jardin Majorelle (Yves Saint Laurent's iconic blue garden and Berber museum) for a serene and photogenic farewell to the city — arrive early to beat the crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the YSL Museum (Musée Yves Saint Laurent Marrakech) adjacent to the Majorelle Garden — a world-class museum celebrating the designer's lifelong love affair with Morocco, housed in a stunning contemporary building. Enjoy a final mint tea or coffee at the Café Bô-Zin or the Majorelle Garden café. Private transfer to Marrakech Menara Airport for your departure flight.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Marrakech. End of a premium 7-day Moroccan journey.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent final breakfast at the riad — full spread of Moroccan pastries, fresh-squeezed orange juice, eggs, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Jardin Majorelle café or at Grand Café de la Poste (Boulevard el Mansour Eddahbi) — a French-Moroccan colonial-era brasserie with excellent salads, sandwiches, and Moroccan dishes; ideal for a relaxed final meal
meals.dinner: Dinner at the airport or on board your return flight (no premium dinner scheduled unless departure is late evening)

day_by_day.notes: The Jardin Majorelle opens at 08:00 — arrive early for the best experience before tour groups arrive. The YSL Museum requires a separate ticket (book online in advance). Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for airport transfer and check-in. Consider purchasing a bottle of premium argan oil or a handcrafted item as a lasting memento. Tip your riad staff before departure — 100–200 MAD per person is appropriate for a week's stay.
